data.label: Invoice upload and review
data.description: Existing staff browser outside provisioning scope. Staff upload PDF invoices, inspect extracted fields alongside source evidence and approve a specific result revision. Propose authenticated staff access with separately authorized reviewer membership.

data.label: Invoice processing and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Amazon ECS. Owns browser/API, background worker, isolated PDF/OCR parser, private versioned Amazon S3 originals, durable PostgreSQL queue/outbox on Amazon RDS, staff sign-in, SQL user/reviewer membership, regional model integration, separate workload identities and operating tasks/monitoring. Accepts PDFs up to 10,000,000 bytes; the proposed 100-page safeguard remains reviewable. Plans for approximately 500 invoices/day; 15,000/month assumes 30 intake days and is not measured usage. Invoices may contain personal data. Extracts supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence into a durable review queue. Approval binds the exact result revision, source and destination contract; model output cannot authorize delivery. Transactional job creation, fenced worker leases and bounded retries preserve processing across failures. Accounting sends use stable operation and payload identity; uncertain outcomes are fenced for reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Destination must independently pass normalized-action-v1 and idempotency acceptance. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement scheduled cleanup and review versions, backups and restore behavior against that requirement; retention eligibility alone does not prove erasure. Propose Sydney ap-southeast-2, not yet user-approved, with documents, extracted data, model processing, logs containing invoice data, backups and state restricted to Australia. No silent overseas inference or recovery fallback. Propose encryption, authorized staff/reviewer access and exclusion of invoice content from operational logs. Accounting residency is unresolved. Service/model availability, quotas, model data-retention policy, destination connectivity, build/scan evidence, restore and alert delivery remain unverified.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without recreation or modification. Receives only approved invoice results. Vendor, hosting and processing locations, authentication and retention behavior are unknown; Australian residency must be established before sending invoice data. Its adapter must pass normalized-action-v1 acceptance, including durable idempotency for repeated operation IDs and reconciliation after ambiguous responses. Compatibility and residency are not established by this diagram.

REQ-001 — must functional other: Accept PDF invoice uploads and durably present supplier, invoice date, total and currency in a review queue. Proposed safeguard: show supporting source evidence and keep failed or uncertain extraction visible for review rather than automatically delivering it. (open)

REQ-002 — must functional security: Send an invoice result to the existing accounting API only after an authorized reviewer approves that exact result revision. Proposed controls bind approval to the source and destination contract, invalidate approval when the result changes and retain an attributable approval/delivery history. (open)

REQ-003 — must nonfunctional reliability: Repeated delivery and retries for the same invoice operation must not create duplicate accounting invoices. Preserve durable operation and payload identity across recovery; reconcile ambiguous external outcomes before resending unless destination idempotency is independently established. Acceptance must cover duplicate delivery, worker interruption and an accounting write followed by a lost response. (open)

REQ-004 — must nonfunctional compliance: Keep invoice documents and extracted data in Australia across storage, processing, inference, backups, recovery and accounting delivery. Proposed controls restrict personal-data access to authorized staff/workloads and exclude invoice content from operational logs. Verify service/model availability and processing geography before use; keep unresolved destinations blocked from receiving invoice data. (open)

REQ-005 — must nonfunctional compliance: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement and verify cleanup across application records and object versions, with documented backup expiry and restoration handling; an exact deletion deadline and retention start event remain to be resolved. [Original and extraction audit retention == 90days] (open)

REQ-006 — must nonfunctional scalability: Support approximately 500 PDF invoices per day through durable intake, extraction and review without losing accepted work. Validate this baseline with representative PDFs and failure recovery; daily volume does not establish peak capacity or processing latency. (open)

We’re designing an AWS invoice workflow that extracts four fields, queues them for review and sends only approved results to your existing accounting API without duplicate invoices. Let’s use one composed application with durable processing and recovery; accounting compatibility still needs testing.

**Which country must invoice data stay in?** This determines where we propose storage and AI processing; for example, “Australia”, “no restriction” or “not sure”.

We’ll design for around 500 invoices a day, PDFs up to 10 MB, personal data and 90-day retention, with documents and extracted data staying in Australia. Let’s propose AWS Sydney (ap-southeast-2), pending your agreement; service/model availability and processing geography remain unverified.
